reset: Reset puts the original onelake.json back.
title: OneLake settings for a workspace: outside apps, SAS tokens, cache and diagnostics
objective_text: Set the OneLake tenant and workspace settings for outside apps, the file explorer, SAS tokens, the shortcut cache and diagnostic events, and predict how each one behaves.
scenario: The Claims workspace needs OneLake opened up to Azure Databricks and a partner app, but security wants the file explorer app blocked. A busy cloud shortcut is costing egress, and the auditors want a record of who reads what.
engine_label: A model of OneLake's tenant and workspace settings, checked on this PC
verifies: Your tenant settings, the OneLake tab of the workspace settings, the SAS token setting and your expectations follow the OneLake file explorer, security, shortcut caching, diagnostics and tenant settings pages, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That any setting changes in Fabric. Nothing is set here.
Whether caching covers ADLS Gen2 or OneLake shortcuts. The shortcuts page lists the types it supports and doesn't name these two.
Immutability of diagnostic events, the end user identifiers setting and outbound access protection.
Security groups that a tenant setting can be limited to.

expected.description: External apps on, file explorer off, short-lived SAS tokens on. On the OneLake tab the cache is on for 14 days and diagnostic events go to AuditLH. The Claims workspace admin turns SAS sign-in on. Spark still reads with external apps off, tokens last at most 1 hour, a changed bucket file is read fresh, Reset cache empties the workspace's cache, the explorer app exits and leaves placeholders, and diagnostics need a Claims admin who's a contributor on the lakehouse.

validation.fail: Databricks would be blocked, or the file explorer app would still sync.
validation.pass: Outside apps can reach OneLake and the file explorer app can't sync.

rules.why: Azure Databricks and custom apps that use the ADLS APIs run outside Fabric. They need this setting.
The file explorer app has its own tenant setting. Turning it off blocks the app even when outside apps are allowed.
With the external apps setting off, users still reach data from apps inside Fabric such as Spark and Data Warehouse.
When the setting is turned off, a running app exits. Placeholders and downloaded files stay on the PC, but nothing syncs.

validation.fail: The partner app can't use SAS tokens in Claims, or you expect the wrong token lifetime.
validation.pass: Short-lived SAS tokens are on, and the Claims workspace admin allows them in Claims.

rules.why: This tenant setting must be on before anyone can get the user delegation keys that sign OneLake SAS tokens.
The setting that lets apps sign in with OneLake SAS tokens is delegated to workspace admins by default.
User delegation keys and OneLake SAS tokens can't last longer than one hour.

validation.fail: The shortcut cache isn't set for two weeks, or it doesn't behave the way you expect.
validation.pass: The cache keeps the bucket's files for two weeks, and you know how it refreshes and resets.

rules.why: Shortcut caching covers Google Cloud Storage, S3, S3 compatible and on-premises gateway shortcuts.
Retention can be 1 to 28 days, and the team wants two weeks.

rules.equals: the newer file from the bucket
rules.why: When the remote store has a newer version, OneLake reads it from there and updates the cache.

rules.equals: every cached file in the workspace
rules.why: Reset cache removes all files from the shortcut cache in the workspace.

validation.fail: Diagnostic events won't reach a lakehouse they can go to, or the wrong person turns them on.
validation.pass: Diagnostic events go to AuditLH on the same capacity, turned on by a Claims admin who can write there.

rules.why: The lakehouse for diagnostic events must be on the same capacity as the workspace.
To turn on diagnostics you must be an admin of the workspace and a contributor on the lakehouse that gets the events.

hints: Does Azure Databricks count as an app inside Fabric or outside it?
The file explorer app and outside apps have separate tenant settings. Can one be on and the other off?
Which OneLake tenant setting can a workspace admin override for their own workspace?
What does the cache do when the file in the bucket is newer than the cached copy?
Where must the diagnostics lakehouse sit, and what role do you need on it?
explanation: Azure Databricks and apps that use the ADLS APIs are outside Fabric, so they need the external apps tenant setting. Spark and Data Warehouse inside Fabric work either way. The file explorer app has a separate setting, so it can be blocked while outside apps are allowed. A running app then exits and leaves its placeholders. OneLake SAS tokens need the short-lived SAS tenant setting, and the setting that lets apps sign in with them is delegated to workspace admins by default. Keys and tokens last one hour at most. The OneLake tab turns on the shortcut cache for 1 to 28 days. A newer remote file is read from the source and replaces the cached copy, and Reset cache empties the whole workspace's cache. Diagnostic events go to a lakehouse on the same capacity, and the person who turns them on is a workspace admin and a contributor on that lakehouse.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-23. get-started-security (last updated 2026-09-01): with the external apps setting on, custom apps using ADLS APIs or the file explorer work. With it off, users still reach data from Spark, Data Engineering and Data Warehouse. service-admin-portal-onelake (last updated 2026-09-29): the external apps setting names ADLS API apps, the file explorer and Databricks. 'Use short-lived user-delegated SAS tokens' must be on to get user delegation keys. 'Authenticate with OneLake user-delegated SAS tokens' is delegated to workspace admins by default. Keys and tokens can't exceed one hour. onelake-file-explorer (last updated 2026-08-17): its own tenant setting, plus the external apps setting. When the setting is turned off a running app exits, and placeholders and downloads stay. onelake-shortcuts (last updated 2026-11-08): cache on the workspace's OneLake tab, retention 1 to 28 days, reset on access, a newer remote version is served from the remote and updates the cache, Reset cache removes all files from the workspace's cache, and the supported types are GCS, S3, S3 compatible and gateway shortcuts. onelake-diagnostics-overview (last updated 2026-05-18): toggle 'Add diagnostic events to a lakehouse' on the workspace's OneLake settings tab, you must be a workspace admin and a contributor to the destination lakehouse, and the lakehouse must be in the same capacity.

Not graded: whether OneLake diagnostics is preview or GA. The page has no preview banner but doesn't say GA, so a reviewer should recheck before the exercise goes live. Also not graded: caching for ADLS Gen2 and OneLake shortcuts (not in the supported list, but not stated as excluded) and the end user identifiers setting.
